title: Specializing cos(A - B) at B = A to Recover the Pythagorean Identity
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: What identity results when you substitute B = A into the cosine difference formula \cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B? Explain how this connects to a fundamental trigonometric identity.

steps.title: Substitute B = A into Both Sides of the Identity
steps.explanation: Replace every occurrence of B with A in cos(A - B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B.
steps.why: An identity valid for all A and B holds in particular when B = A.

steps.title: Simplify Both Sides
steps.explanation: On the left side, A - A = 0; on the right side, the products become squares.
steps.why: Any real number minus itself is 0, and x*x = x^2.

steps.title: Evaluate cos 0 to Obtain the Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Since cos 0 = 1, the equation reduces to cos^2 A + sin^2 A = 1, which agrees with the fundamental Pythagorean identity.
steps.why: At angle 0 on the unit circle, the point is (1, 0), so cos 0 = 1.
